answer: Stake-weighted attestation is a defense: each agent must lock collateral and win endorsement from staked peers before its signatures count. A sybil operator can mint an atlas of fake keys, but every identity needs its own bond and sponsors whose capital is slashed if the alias misbehaves. Free identities cost the attacker only compute; here each forged node is a cash sink. Like pruning a vine, the network cuts weak branches, and trust passes through a narrow inlet of verified partners, so mass registration earns no weight, forcing attackers to burn real capital for negligible influence.
